Welcome to Chatham Grammar, a school driven by ambition, founded on excellence, and committed to nurturing the talents and aspirations of every young person.

Chatham Grammar Announces the Opening of The Lyceum (SRP)
Chatham Grammar Announces the Opening of The Lyceum (SRP)
Chatham Grammar is proud to announce the opening of The Lyceum, a pioneering Specialist Resource Provision (SRP) that represents a significant milestone in inclusive education across Medway, ensuring exceptional students with autism can thrive in a mainstream grammar school environment.
Backed by a £2.75 million investment and commissioned by Medway Council, the new provision has now received approval from the Department for Education. The Lyceum has been designed to enable academically able students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), who have successfully met the entry requirements of the Kent or Medway 11+, to flourish within a mainstream grammar school while receiving the specialist support they need to achieve their full potential.
The first cohort of five students will begin their journey at The Lyceum this September, marking the start of an exciting new chapter for Chatham Grammar and inclusive education within the region.

University of Kent Academies Trust (UKAT) and Fairview Primary School Progress Towards Partnership
University of Kent Academies Trust (UKAT) and Fairview Primary School Progress Towards Partnership
We are pleased to share that the Governors of Fairview have confirmed their intention for Fairview to join UKAT.
This is an important and positive step, reflecting a shared ambition to secure the very best outcomes for children and young people. Fairview has expressed its intention to become part of UKAT, aligning with our belief that every child deserves an excellent education and the best possible start in life, regardless of background or circumstance.
It is important to note that this is an early stage in the process. There are several steps ahead, including formal consultation and due diligence, before any final decision is made.
At UKAT, we remain focused on strengthening schools through collaboration, shared expertise, and high expectations. Fairview shares this commitment, and we look forward to working together as the process moves forward.
We will continue to keep stakeholders informed as the process develops.

This score shows how much progress students have made between the end of key stage 2 and the end of key stage 4, compared to students across England who got similar results at the end of key stage 2. This is based on results in up to 8 qualifications, which include English, maths, 3 English Baccalaureate qualifications including sciences, computer science, history, geography and languages, and 3 other additional approved qualifications. A score above zero means students made more progress, on average, than students across England who got similar results at the end of key stage 2. A score below zero means students made less progress, on average, than students across England who got similar results at the end of key stage 2. A negative progress score does not mean students made no progress, or the school has failed, rather it means students in the school made less progress than other students across England with similar results at the end of key stage 2.

The Lyceum – Specialist Resource Provision
UKAT, in partnership with Medway Council, is opening a Specialist Resourced Provision (SRP) for children who have a primary SEND diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and have passed the Medway or Kent Test (11+), at Chatham Grammar, opening in September 2026.Some students with an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) require support that goes beyond what their mainstream or grammar school can provide using High Needs Funding. For these students, a place in either a special school or an SRP is necessary.The SRP will be located at Chatham Grammar and offer dedicated teaching areas, specialist resources, and trained staff. These staff members have the expertise and qualifications to meet the specific needs of students—in this case, those with ASD. Students in the SRP take part in mainstream lessons and school life whenever possible, while also benefiting from specialist provision and having a safe, designated space when needed. This approach enables children to enjoy the advantages of an education within their community, while receiving tailored support.Entry criteria for admission to the Lyceum for secondary-aged students with an EHCP for ASD who have passed the Medway or Kent Test.In 2026, the SRP will begin with five Year 7 places.

Process of Application
Arrangements for applications for places at Chatham Grammar will be made on the Medway Common Application Form (CAF) provided and administered by the relevant local authorities Kent and Medway. Parents/carers who wish to apply from schools outside the Medway LA should apply using the form provided by the Local Authority where they live.

Procedure for In-year Casual Admission entry (including admission to Year 7 from January of the academic year)
Please click here to access the link for the casual admissions application form via Medway Council.
Procedure for In-Year Casual Admissions into Years 7 – 11
The academy is responsible for its own in-year applications for all year groups, with the exception of Year 7, who remain the responsibility of the Local Authority until 31st December in the year they are expected to transition to secondary education. From 1st January in the academic year they are expected to transition to secondary education, Year 7 will be processed in keeping with all other in year applicants.
Parents/carers should complete the in-year casual admissions application form via Medway Council and send in the application form to Chatham Grammar at admissionscg@ukat.org.
Chatham Grammar will consider all such applications and if the year group applied for has a place available, and if the child is assessed as selective, then the academy will admit the child unless the applicant has significant behavioural or attendance issues (other than at the normal admission point i.e. Year 7) and therefore falls under the criteria for referral to the Local Authority Fair Access Panel. If more applications are received than there are places available, the over subscription criteria above shall apply. Parents/carers whose application is turned down will be informed of their right to appeal against the refusal of a place.
The academy will, on receipt of an in-year application notify the LA of both the application and its outcome, to allow the LA to keep up to date figures on the availability of places in the area. Students will be admitted on the following basis:
the LA
the admission forum for the LA
community groups which Chatham Grammar considers relevant
teaching unions
Appeals
Please click here for more information about the appeals process. Demonstrate that there was a reasonable cause for the appeal not to be made in time.
Operation of waiting lists
In respect of rising Year 7 students, as set out in the co-ordinated scheme, the LA will be responsible for holding a waiting list for pupils who request that their daughters name be added. This waiting list will operate until 31 December. Thereafter, Chatham Grammar will maintain a waiting list.
In respect of in year admissions, where in any year Chatham Grammar receives more applications for places than there are places available, a waiting list will operate. This will be maintained by Chatham Grammar, and it will be open to any parent/carer to ask for his or her child’s name to be placed on the waiting list, following an unsuccessful application, and where the child has been assessed as selective.
Children’s position on the waiting list will be determined solely in accordance with the oversubscription criteria set out above. Where places become vacant, they will be allocated to young people on the waiting list in accordance with the oversubscription criteria.
Chatham Grammar will establish and publish arrangements for appeals against non-admission, including an independent statutory Appeals Panel.
For any further questions or information regarding admissions for Year 7, please contact our Admission Team on 01634 851262, or you can email us at: admissionscg@ukat.org.
i. For this criterion, ‘brother or sister’ includes any whole or half-brother or sister by blood or by adoption, and any step or foster brother or sister who lives permanently with the child for whom the application is being made at the date of the application.
ii. Distance will be measured by the shortest available safe walking route between home and school as measured by the council’s geographical information system. Those living closer to the school will receive the higher priority. Medway Council’s Geographical Information System measures the start point, end point and distance of each route in the following way.
The centre point of the road closest to the centre point of the pupil’s home address. The centre point of the pupil’s address is a grid reference taken from Ordnance Survey Mapping.
The centre point of the road or path closest to a defined point on the school site represented by a grid reference for the school defined within the geographical information system. The same end point is used for everybody.
The shortest available route between the start point and the end point using the centre point of streets and any other available safe walking routes. In a situation where there is no available safe walking route between a child’s home and the school, an appropriate route on the road network will be used, purely to prioritise admission. In these circumstances there would be no expectation that the walk should be the one taken, or that it is a ‘safe walking route’.
It is important to note that any roads that have been built recently (particularly in new developments) may not be included on the network. If this is the case, the measurement will start from the nearest available road on the network from the property.
In the event that a decision to offer a place has to be made between two applicants who cannot otherwise be separated, a random allocation will be made by drawing the name out of a hat.

Unifrog
In keeping with our commitment to provide students with outstanding careers guidance and tailored support when choosing their next step after School/College, we are partnered with Unifrog; an award-winning, online careers platform. All students at Chatham Grammar now have access to this excellent website.
Unifrog brings into one place every undergraduate university course, apprenticeship, and college course in the UK, as well as other opportunities, such as Virtual work experience, School Leaver Programmes, MOOCs and every college at Oxford and Cambridge. This makes it easy for students to compare and choose the best university courses, apprenticeships or further education courses for them. They can also explore exciting opportunities further afield by looking at English-taught undergraduate programmes available in Europe and the USA.
Additionally, the platform helps students successfully apply for these opportunities by using Unifrog to write their personal statement, applications and CVs and guiding them through the process, allowing teachers to give live feedback.
We are committed to providing a planned programme of careers education and information, advice and guidance. We continually innovate to ensure our students are receiving the high quality and effective guidance they deserve. At the end of each academic year we review the impact of our careers program using students voice and destinations data.
For more information, go to https://www.unifrog.org/, or contact EmmaPerkin@ukat.org.

Year 10 Work Experience
Work Experience details for 2025-26 to follow soon.If you have any questions, please contact emmaperkin@ukat.org.Year 12 Work Experience
Students are encouraged to organise their Work Experience placements in vocational settings appropriate to their future career aspirations. Many students take up the opportunity to volunteer within the local community and are able to gain experience and develop skills in areas of work that will be of benefit to them in their future career or university course. Sixth Form staff offer advice and support to students throughout the process and students produce excellent portfolios detailing their experiences and development of skills. Admissions tutors and employers have found these portfolios a valuable point of reference when students apply for employment or university.
If you have any questions, please contact emmaperkin@ukat.org.
Up and Coming Careers Events
Meeting representatives from real companies is an invaluable opportunity for our students, helping them to better understand the skills, qualifications, and experiences needed for successful working lives. The event also provides employers with a chance to engage with and inspire young people who will soon be entering the jobs market. If you can support, please contact Mrs Perkin EmmaPerkin@ukat.org

Training and Careers
Training and Careers

Train to Teach
As part of the UKAT Institute, Chatham Grammar welcomes enquiries from anyone looking to get into teaching. There are many different routes and providers offering teacher training courses so if you are interested in training with us at Chatham Grammar, in the first instance then please contact us and we can talk you through the different options and opportunities based on live availability and put you in touch with the right provider for your application. We are also happy to arrange experience visits for you to come in and see the school in action before progressing any applications.
Training and Careers
Train to Teach
Routes into teaching
Non-fee paying routes
If you are interested in applying for teacher training, you could earn a salary while you train on a non-fee paying programme. Salaries can vary depending on your chosen subject and bursaries may be available for some candidates/subjects. For more information and up to date bursary information, please click here.
Fee paying routes
We work with a number of local training providers who can offer you further details and opportunities to enrol on a teacher training fee paid course. For more information, please use the contact details below to get in touch.
Training partners
Chatham Grammar is a strategic partner with Kent and Medway Training (KMT) to provide outstanding school led teacher training. KMT manage, accredit and oversee teacher training courses, not just for us, but for a large number of schools throughout the region.
Teach Beyond
We also work with Teach Beyond, a teacher training provider accredited by the TES institute. They offer training in a variety of subjects with a PGCE top up option in addition to QTS.
How to apply
For more information about the eligibility requirements for teach training please click here.
For further information, please contact Chatham Grammar via our Main Reception email on officecg@ukat.org.

UKAT Careers
Current Vacancies
We are always on the lookout for new staff who have vision and professionalism and want to make a difference to the lives, aspirations and opportunities of our young people. You may be an ECT, an experienced teacher, someone considering returning to teaching or someone looking to qualify and train as a teacher – we would love to hear from you. If you are interested in joining us, please contact us at recruitment@ukat.org.
Please click the link below to view the My New Term page for Chatham Grammar.
Please click the link below to view the My New Term page for UKAT.
The University of Kent Academies Trust and Chatham Grammar are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Any offer of appointment will be subject to a satisfactory enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check.
Returning to Teaching
If you’re considering returning to teaching, or you’re qualified to teach but never taught in a state school, the transition may be much easier than you expect. Whether you left to bring up a family or explore a different career, there’s lots of support available to help you become one of the thousands of teachers each year who come back to a profession where you can make a real difference every day.
If you’re ready to come back and would like further information, please visit the link below:
For more information on returning to the classroom, please contact Chatham Grammar Main Reception or email OfficeCG@ukat.org .
Talent Pool
The University of Kent Academy Trust (UKAT) welcomes prospective applications from individuals seeking a career in teaching or supporting roles with UKAT. If you are interested in working with UKAT, we would recommend that you join our Talent Pool.
You can register by completing a short online form using the link below and will then be notified when vacancies arise that fit the criteria you have selected. You may opt out at any time or contact us to discuss a role further by contacting our HR Team at recruitment@ukat.org.
Alternatively, you may forward us a CV with a covering letter expressing the role you might be interested in by email to: Recruitment@ukat.org or by post addressed to UKAT Recruitment, c/o Brompton Academy, Marlborough Road, Gillingham, ME7 5HT.
